input.context: captureTee appends one JSON line per trial to a per-agent JSONL file via fileStore.put(). If the process is killed (SIGKILL, OOM) mid-write, the file can end up with a truncated final line — valid JSONL up to the last complete line, garbage after. Every downstream reader (crew:gepa-history, detectEvalDriftFromSplits, the soak monitor) needs to keep working against a file that might have exactly one corrupted trailing line, without losing the valid trials before it.
constraints: fileStore is the only write path — no separate WAL or journal exists today
Readers are read-only Node ESM scripts, no daemon process babysitting the file
Fix must not require a schema change to gepa-core's Trial type or a new dependency

expected_output.summary: Readers parse line-by-line and skip (with a logged warning, not a throw) any line that fails JSON.parse or fails a minimal shape check — treating the file as 'valid JSONL prefix, best-effort suffix' rather than requiring the whole file to be well-formed; a corrupted trailing line is invisible to scoring (dropped, not crashed on) and the next successful write appends a fresh valid line after it
expected_output.non_goals_explicit: Does not add an atomic-write (temp+rename) path to fileStore in this design — that would prevent the corruption but changes the hot-write-path contract and needs its own spike; this design accepts corruption can happen and focuses on graceful read-side recovery
failure_modes_named: A corrupted line lands in the middle of the file, not just the trailing line (e.g. two concurrent captureTee writes interleave) — line-by-line parsing still isolates it correctly since JSONL corruption from a torn write only ever affects the specific write in flight, not neighboring completed lines

Silent line-skipping without a visible warning means small-scale corruption is invisible until someone notices a trial count mismatch — the skip must emit a structured log line so it is observable, not just safe

dependencies_graphed.reader_shim: a shared parseJsonlSafe(path) helper used by crew:gepa-history, detectEvalDriftFromSplits' caller, and the soak monitor — one implementation, not three copies
dependencies_graphed.logging: skip events logged via the existing observability-events.ts pattern (gepa_capture_drop sibling event, e.g. gepa_trial_parse_skip)

expected_output.test_strategy_present: Unit: fixture file with 5 valid lines + 1 truncated trailing line parses to 5 trials, skipped: 1, one log line emitted; unit: fixture with a corrupted line in the middle behaves identically (5 valid + 1 skipped, order preserved for the valid ones)
expected_output.tradeoffs_articulated: Atomic temp+rename writes were considered as the 'fix it at the source' alternative and explicitly deferred, not rejected — it is the more complete fix but changes the write-hot-path (extra rename syscall per trial, plus directory-listing changes for tooling that globs the trials dir) and warrants its own spike rather than riding along on this FEAT's held-out-set expansion work

notes: hand-seed 2026-07-02 FEAT-210 — held-out set expansion for detectEvalDrift minSampleSize; failure_recovery_design scenario, distinct from existing 8 seeds.
